claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the exported function returns their unsigned greatest common divisor as a 32-bit result.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: It covers every pair of 32-bit inputs and returns their unsigned greatest common divisor, including when either or both inputs are zero.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, each interpreted as an unsigned natural number for the greatest-common-divisor calculation.
The result is the greatest common divisor encoded as a 32-bit value; the result conversion wraps modulo 2 to the 32nd power.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the export returns the input selected by nested signed comparisons against the two bounds.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The nested signed comparisons implement the stated rule: return `lo` if `x` is below it, otherwise `hi` if `x` is above it, otherwise `x`.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit inputs, interpreted as signed two's-complement values for the comparisons.

Returns the lower bound when the input is signed-less than it; otherwise returns the upper bound when the upper bound is signed-less than the input; otherwise returns the input. The returned bit pattern is one of the inputs, with no arithmetic wraparound.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly that selected input.
caveats: The comparisons are signed, but there is no stated requirement that the lower bound be less than or equal to the upper bound; for reversed bounds the claim specifies the nested comparison behavior rather than a conventional clamp contract.
